title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit

reading.body:
The failure here is an expert witness using a general-purpose AI tool to generate a report that was prompted to reach a predetermined legal conclusion. The prompt, as revealed in court documents, instructed the system to show a party was zero percent at fault before any analysis had taken place. This is not a case of an AI system malfunctioning on its own terms. It is a case of a human deploying a tool outside the conditions it was built for, using it to produce advocacy disguised as independent expert analysis.

The point of failure is at the human-AI interface, not inside the model itself. Expert testimony is supposed to reflect the independent judgment of a qualified witness. The prompting behavior described here bypassed that function entirely, treating the AI as a drafting tool for a conclusion already chosen. A standard check, meaning any adversarial review of how the report was produced, was apparently what ultimately exposed the problem, since the prompts themselves surfaced in discovery.

What is not established is whether the expert's conclusions were factually wrong, whether any court has ruled the report inadmissible, or whether any finding of misconduct has been made. The reporting describes embarrassment and the existence of the prompts, not a legal determination about their effect on the proceedings or the underlying liability question.

reports.title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit

summary:
An expert witness hired by 3M to defend the company in a lawsuit over a deadly Houston explosion used ChatGPT to write major portions of his expert report. Court documents revealed that the witness asked the AI tool to create a report showing that 3M was zero percent at fault for the 2020 explosion at Watson Grinding facility, which killed three people and damaged around 200 homes. The incident demonstrates how artificial intelligence has infiltrated courtrooms through expert testimony, not just legal briefs and other documents.

The Watson Grinding explosion was caused by a degraded rubber welding hose that leaked flammable gas, according to investigators. Homeowners and others sued 3M and Watson Grinding, claiming 3M failed to properly maintain the facility's gas detection system and made other errors contributing to the disaster. The case involves multiple deaths and hundreds of millions of dollars in total liability. The discovery of the AI prompts used to create the expert report proved embarrassing to the defense, showing how the testimony was artificially crafted to support a predetermined outcome.
